t:
(a) Section 104(a) of the Manpower Development and Training Act of 1962 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) is amended by striking out “1967” and inserting in lieu thereof “1968”. 
    (b) Section 105 of the Act is amended by striking out “1967” where it appears in the first sentence and inserting in lieu thereof “1968”, and by amending the last sentence thereof to read as follows: “Of the funds appropriated for a fiscal year to carry out this Act, not more than $300,000 may be used for purposes of this section.”

fable.w: The section only changes dates from 1967 to 1968 in two provisions of the Manpower Development and Training Act and caps the funds usable for one section at $300,000. The tempting reading is that the amended sections 104 and 105 might themselves involve outside advisory or consultation processes, but nothing in this text creates or requires any consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into a federal decision here.
fable.s: Of the funds appropriated for a fiscal year to carry out this Act, not more than $300,000 may be used for purposes of this section.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to dates and funding caps within existing statutes. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely administrative and legislative housekeeping.

opus.w: The section only changes "1967" to "1968" in Sections 104 and 105 of the Manpower Development and Training Act and caps funding for Section 105. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. That the underlying act deals with outside workers and programs is not enough, because this text sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: Of the funds appropriated for a fiscal year to carry out this Act, not more than $300,000 may be used for purposes of this section.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes": the Manpower Development and Training Act involves outside trainees and programs. But this section only changes dates and sets a funding cap. It sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section contains only technical amendments to dates and funding caps within the Manpower Development and Training Act. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private organizations. The changes are purely legislative adjustments to existing statutory parameters.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the Act implies some form of legislative participation or public input, but the text itself only describes technical amendments to dates and funding limits. There is no mention of public comment, hearings, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with non-federal entities. The actors involved are Congress (amending the statute) and the federal agency (using funds), both of which are inside the government.
